newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to start full probe into Anglo's Lonrho stake.
newsitem.headline: EU to start full probe into Anglo's Lonrho stake.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to start on Monday an in-depth, four-month probe into South African mining giant Anglo American's stake in British-based Lonrho Plc, an industry source said on Friday.
"Short of (European Competition Commissioner Karel) Van Miert changing his mind, it will go into second phase," the source told Reuters on the condition of anonymity.
Van Miert usually follows the proposal of DGIV, the competition directorate-general.
The decision to open a detailed probe is hardly surprising after the Commission blocked in April the merger of the platinum interests of Gencor, also South African, and Lonrho.
Van Miert said at the time the deal would create a duopoly between the new company and Anglo's Amplats in the world market for platinum and warned Anglo against taking control of Lonrho.

Despite the warning, Anglo did precisely that by acquiring Lonrho chief executive Dieter Bock's 18.4 percent stake recently. It now controls approximately 29 percent of Lonrho, which under the European Union's merger rules gives it control of the company.

Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson has argued that, due to the Commission's objections, it was never his intention "to interfere with Lonrho's platinum operations". But it is unclear what he means to do to avoid exerting control.
Lonrho owns 73 percent of its platinum division. Gencor owns the rest.
Both the European Commission and Lohnro declined to comment on the report.

Ogilvie Thompson has said he is hopeful a compromise will be found with the Commission, which must vet all large mergers and acquisitions involving companies which do important business in the EU irrespective of whether they are European or not.
Van Miert also noted recently that Anglo was willing to discuss the competition problems posed by its significant stake in Lonrho, hinting that the operation was not in real danger.
The Commission must rule by Monday night whether to clear the deal after its preliminary one-month probe or open a full investigation.
Platinum is a precious metal used particularly in jewellery and in the making of car catalytic converters.
Gencor, Anglo and Lonrho control more than 60 percent of the world's total output.
